newsitem.title: USA: Golden Books offers to buy Canadian TV producer.
newsitem.headline: Golden Books offers to buy Canadian TV producer.

text.p: Golden Books Family Entertainment said Wednesday it is negotiating to buy Canadian children's television producer Nelvana Limited for $102 million (C$140 million).
Toronto-based Nelvana's animated television series include Babar, Rupert, The Adventures of Tintin, Little Bear, Care Bears, and such live-action series as Nancy Drew and the Hardy Boys.

"It is through mergers like this that we believe we can realise our strategy of building a focused family entertainment company across all media," said Richard Snyder, chairman and chief executive officer of Golden Books Family Entertainment.
Golden Books, a leading publisher of children's books and hobby books, recently purchased Broadway Video.

"We can join Nelvana's 600-episode library with that of Golden Books and our recent Broadway Video acquisition, and further leverage Nelvana's strong animation production capabilities through additional character development," Snyder said in a statement.
Under the proposed deal, Golden Books would pay $19.71 (C$27.00) per share in cash and stock for all outstanding shares of Nelvana. The mix of cash and Golden Books stock has yet to be determined.

The transaction is subject to the completion of due diligence, the negotiation of a definitive merger agreement, approval by the boards of Golden Books and Nelvana, approval by Nelvana's shareholders and regulatory approvals. The companies said they hope to complete the merger by the end of October.
Golden Books stock was up 50 cents to $11.75 in early trading on Nasdaq. Nilvana traded at C$28, off C30 cents, on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
